title: Algorithms & Data Structures: Sorting and Searching
welcome_lead: Compare classic algorithms by speed, stability and memory.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: merge sort, quicksort, bubble sort, linear and binary search.
final_note: Know the trade-offs — there is no single best algorithm.

concepts.def: A divide-and-conquer sort with O(n log n) time complexity.
A divide-and-conquer sort averaging O(n log n), worst O(n^2).
A simple comparison sort with O(n^2) time complexity.
O(log n) search on a sorted array by repeated halving.

walkthroughs.body_html: Merge sort is O(n log n) in all cases but needs O(n) extra space. Quicksort is O(n log n) on average and in-place, but O(n^2) on bad pivots. Bubble sort is O(n^2) and only useful for teaching.
Linear search is O(n) and works on any list. Binary search is O(log n) but requires the data to be sorted. Doubling the input adds only one extra comparison to binary search.
Use binary search when the array is sorted. Use quicksort for in-place speed. Use merge sort when stability or guaranteed O(n log n) matters. Bubble sort survives only in textbooks.
